Article Title: ‘Bharat is one, and will be forever’: VP Radhakrishnan flags off Tiranga bike rally in Delhi, NDA MPs participate
Article Text:
NDA MPs participate in 'Tiranga Yatra' rally in Delhi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan on Wednesday flagged off a “Har Ghar Tiranga” bike rally in the national capital ahead of Independence Day celebrations on August 15.The rally, organised as part of the ongoing “Har Ghar Tiranga” campaign, saw participation from MPs of the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and a large number of supporters carrying the national flag. The rally is scheduled to cover the stretch from Bharat Mandapam to Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium.Addressing participants, Radhakrishnan noted that the various activities organised under the campaign may differ in form but carry the same sentiment of national belonging.“In Tiranga Yatra, bike rallies, cultural programmes, the activities are different but the sentiment they carry is the same, that is the collective sense of belonging... I urge each one of you to actively engage in this campaign and inspire every citizen to hoist the Tricolour with pride,” ANI quoted him as saying.The vice president also emphasised the unity of the country, declaring, “Bharat is one, and it will be one forever.”He paid tribute to Pingali Venkayya, who designed the national flag, and recalled Hansa Mehta, who led a group of 72 women who presented the first National Flag of independent India to Dr Rajendra Prasad, the country’s first president.Several NDA MPs attended the rally. BJP MP Tarun Chugh highlighted the enthusiasm of young people and their resolve to contribute towards the goal of a developed India.“Under the leadership of PM Modi, the youth have come out today with the resolution of ‘Viksit Bharat’. Tiranga is the pride of India. Under PM Modi, India will realise the resolve to become a developed India,” Chugh said.Union minister of state for Home Nityanand Rai highlighted the significance of the national flag, describing the Tricolour as a sentiment deeply connected with the country and its people.“The Tiranga is our pride, and it is more precious to us than our life,” Rai said.BJP MP Ramvir Singh Bidhuri pointed to the participation of a large number of MPs in response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for the Tiranga Yatra.“In response to PM Modi's call, a large number of MPs are joining this Tiranga Yatra today, and the Vice President will inaugurate this Tiranga Yatra. The journey will go from Bharat Mandapam to the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, and a spectacular celebration is visible here,” Bidhuri said.The “Har Ghar Tiranga” campaign is being held across the country ahead of Independence Day, encouraging citizens, public representatives and organisations to display the national flag.The Delhi rally is part of a series of programmes being organised in the capital to mark Independence Day, with the Tricolour at the centre of celebrations aimed at strengthening the sense of unity and national pride.
Article Summary: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan flagged off a 'Har Ghar Tiranga' bike rally in Delhi. The rally saw participation from MPs of the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and a large number of supporters carrying the national flag. The Delhi rally is part of a series of programmes being organised in the capital to mark Independence Day.

Article Title: Medical device industry seeks rethink of draft law, urges separate regulatory body
Article Text:
The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. (Representative Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The domestic medical device industry, along with hospitals and healthcare providers, has urged govt to re-examine the Draft Drugs, Medical Devices & Cosmetics Bill, 2026."The Bill in its present form, does not provide the regulatory foundation required for India's medical devices sector to grow, innovate, and compete globally", an industry expert told TOI.The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and consolidate laws related to import, manufacture, distribution and sale of drugs, medical devices and cosmetics, to ensure their quality, safety and efficacy.In a letter to govt, the associations say that the draft bill, in its current form, treats medical devices as an adjunct to pharmaceuticals, despite clear scientific, engineering, and regulatory distinction between the two.Medical devices are engineering products, and should not be clubbed with pharmaceuticals, the letter says, adding the draft Bill continues to use drug-centric terminology such as "adulterated", "spurious"."misbranded", and applies pharma-style criminalisation to engineering deviations.Globally, medical devices are regulated through risk-based conformity assessment and quality management systems.Further, the Bill does not provide for a dedicated regulatory authority for medical devices, despite repeated recommendations.In 2023, the Association of Indian Medical Device Industry argued that proposed overarching legislation (such as the Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics draft) fails the domestic sector by continuing to regulate medical devices as "drugs" under a joint framework, instead of establishing an independent, specialized regulatory body.Administrative enforcement including recalls, corrective actions, civil penalties-- should replace imprisonment for technical lapses, the letter by 11 associations including Aimed, AHPI (Association of Healthcare Providers India), ADMI (Association of Diagnostics Manufacturers) and Patient Safety and Access Initiative, says.The Bill 2026 applies uniform penalties across all device classes, from low-risk surgical instruments to high-risk implants, contrary to global norms.It does not clearly recognise key medical device standards covering areas such as biocompatibility, usability and software safety.While the draft has been circulated to various ministries and departments, key stakeholders, including industry associations, manufacturers and hospital bodies, have not been adequately involved in the process, the industry executive said, adding it appears inconsistent with the pre-legislative consultation process.
Article Summary: The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. It would consolidate laws related to import, manufacture, distribution and sale of drugs, medical devices and cosmetics. The domestic medical device industry, along with hospitals and healthcare providers, has urged govt to re-examine the draft.

Article Title: 'Much more to this than meets the eye': Rahul targets PM Modi after US court drops case against Adani
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday reacted sharply to Gautam Adani 's acquittal by a US court and targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the development.In a post on X, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha said, "There is much more to this than meets the eye. A compromised PM was forced to sell India’s interest. India is paying a huge price. "A US federal judge in New York on Monday dismissed the nearly two-year-old criminal case against Adani and the other accused. The US Department of Justice had sought dismissal of the charges, citing six “overlapping bases”, including that the case involved foreign conduct, India had not found “actionable misconduct”, no money had been lost on securities issued and there were “extraordinary proof problems”.The case, filed in November 2024, accused Adani, his nephew Sagar Adani and six others of conspiracy to bribe Indian government officials to secure a solar power contract. The Adani Group had denied the allegations and said its companies and executives had acted in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements.Judge Nicholas Garaufis had earlier questioned the DOJ's decision to drop the case and sought further explanation for the move.The DOJ had argued that the defendants were foreign nationals who had never appeared in the US and were unlikely to do so.Adani, meanwhile, welcomed the court's decision, saying: “Throughout this challenging period, our faith in truth, fairness and the rule of law remained unwavering. My deepest gratitude to those who never lost faith in us, in the system and in India’s capacity for justice,” according to the supplied text.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday reacted sharply to Gautam Adani's acquittal by a US court. He targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the development. A US federal judge in New York on Monday dismissed the nearly two- year-old criminal case against Adani and the other accused.

Article Title: Parl Panel flags shortfall in achieving even 25% of skill development targets under action plan for persons with disabilities
Article Text:
​Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities

NEW DELHI: The parliamentary standing committee on social justice and empowerment has brought into focus the failure of the National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities (NAP-SDP) to meet setout targets and highlighted that the continued shortfall in achieving even 25% of the set targets is a matter of serious concern.The panel in its latest report tabled in Parliament on Monday yet again raised the issue which it had flagged in its earlier report in March saying that the performance of the action plan remained significantly below the set targets over the last three years.In the report on the action taken by the government on the observations and recommendations made in March on ‘Demands for Grants (2026-27)’ of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, the panel said that it has not accepted the reply of the govt on NAP-SDP and added that it requires reiteration.The Committee, in its original report, had observed with concern that under the (NAP-SDP) the performance data reveals a widening gap. Against a target of 17,000 in 2023–24, the Department trained 9,333 beneficiaries; this fell sharply to 836 trainees against a target of 15,000 in 2024–25. Though higher than the previous year in 2025-2026 as of January 2,264 beneficiaries were trained against a target of 10,000.The panel chaired by BJP MP in Lok Sabha PC while acknowledging the administrative challenges posed by the transition to the PM DAKSH-DEPwD portal and the Hybrid Treasury Single Account (TSA) model, had said that the continued shortfall in achieving even 25% of the set targets was cited as a matter of serious concern.With the newly announced Divyangjan Kaushal Yojana, the Committee recommended that the Department adopt a more robust, industry-linked approach to bridge the gap between training and gainful employment. “It is essential that the Department prioritize the placement of certified trainees by strengthening partnerships with private employers and ensuring that training modules remain aligned with current market demands,” the committee had recommended.The Committee had further suggested that the targets for the 2026–27 fiscal year be monitored quarterly to ensure that the transition to the new Yojana results in a measurable improvement in both the number of beneficiaries trained and their subsequent placement in sustainable employment.The Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities in its reply to the Commission dated June 18 said that “the recommendations of the Committee have been noted”. “The new skilling scheme is being designed to address diverse skilling needs and aspirations of all types of Persons with Disabilities, through industry-linked and outcome-based livelihood models. The Department envisages to regularly monitor and review the scheme. ”
Article Summary: Parliamentary standing committee on social justice and empowerment has brought into focus the failure of the National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities (NAP-SDP) to meet setout targets. The panel in its latest report tabled in Parliament on Monday yet again raised the issue which it had flagged in its earlier report.

Article Title: Number of govt elementary schools down 10,000 in a year
Article Text:
Data showed the number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The number of govt elementary schools across the country fell by nearly 10,000 in a year, with Meghalaya, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh recording the steepest declines, according to data tabled in the Lok Sabha on Monday.UDISE+ data showed that the number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26 - a reduction of 9,866 schools, or about 1.1%.The govt data was provided in response to a question from DMK MP T R Baalu on whether a large number of elementary schools had been closed because of insufficient student strength and the steps being taken to prevent dropouts. However, the education ministry did not specify how many of the schools were actually closed due to lack of students, while furnishing the overall number of govt elementary schools in the two academic years.Meghalaya recorded the biggest numerical decline, with the number of govt elementary schools falling from 7,633 to 5,459, a drop of 2,174. Telangana followed with a reduction of 1,961 schools, from 22,983 to 21,022, while Andhra Pradesh saw its count decline by 1,446, from 37,449 to 36,003.Madhya Pradesh had 1,043 fewer schools, Karnataka 615, West Bengal 587, Rajasthan 473 and Maharashtra 357. Himachal Pradesh recorded a decline of 259 schools, while Assam had 209 fewer.Uttar Pradesh, which continues to have the largest network of govt elementary schools, saw the number fall marginally from 1,34,115 to 1,33,948.Not every state recorded a decline. Bihar's count rose from 66,803 to 66,915, while Chhattisgarh increased from 43,836 to 43,853. The numbers remained unchanged in Jammu & Kashmir, Puducherry and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.The ministry said opening, closing and rationalisation of schools fall within the jurisdiction of state and UT govts since education is on the Concurrent List.At the same time, it said access to schooling had improved. The Gross Access Ratio rose between 2018-19 and 2025-26 from 96.49 to 98.14 at upper-primary level, from 88.24 to 95.05 at secondary level and from 65.05 to 94.79 at higher-secondary level.The Centre said states were being supported through Samagra Shiksha and PM POSHAN, besides assistance for school infrastructure, residential schools and hostels, transport facilities, enrolment drives, textbooks and uniforms to curb dropouts and improve enrolment.
Article Summary: Number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26. Meghalaya, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh recorded the steepest declines.

Article Title: Phuket-Delhi Air India pilot fails 2nd dope test, was high on marijuana
Article Text:
Multiple sources told TOI that the PIC was acting under the influence of psychoactive substances.

Airbus A320 had momentarily gone into ‘negative G’ situation

What happened on board

What govt is doing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What it means for AI

NEW DELHI: Trouble mounted for the pilot-in-command (PIC) of last Tuesday’s badly rattled Phuket-Delhi Air India flight after it emerged that he had failed the confirmatory dope test and was found to have consumed marijuana. Besides, the cabin crew of the flight, AI 2379, has filed a complaint with the airline against the “high” PIC’s onboard behaviour.The pilot also faces criminal action beyond DGCA rules — which require such a pilot to be sent for de-addiction and allow him to resume flying after being certified drug-free.The young co-pilot had to single-handedly steady the aircraft and then land it safely at the destination.An alarmed civil aviation ministry summoned AI’s outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson to express concern about this incident and find out how the airline was dealing with the issue and review its plan to come out of its prolonged period of operational turbulence.The incident that has raised questions over the robustness of the Indian system has also pushed DGCA to explore ways to make dope test rules more stringent after the incident that left 20 passengers and four cabin crew members injured.“Certain records, statements, medical information and other material collected during the investigation are protected and confidential in accordance with the applicable investigation framework….AAIB (Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau) requests all concerned to respect the investigation process and refrain from drawing conclusions… AAIB will conduct a thorough investigation covering all material facts and relevant evidence and will issue its preliminary findings,” the aviation ministry said in a statement while responding to queries on the confirmatory test.Multiple sources told TOI that the PIC was acting under the influence of psychoactive substances. “He was often sitting on the floor of the flight deck and tried to smoke out. Cabin crew had to help him back to his seat. He was not in full control of himself. He was unable to walk properly after exiting the aircraft,” said a person in the know. AI did not comment on the cabin crew’s alleged complaints.The probe will determine whether the aircraft had a sudden loss of altitude due to a series of multiple and rare technical snags, which have been reported by the co-pilot in his report, or it was caused by actions of the PIC.When the aircraft experienced loss of altitude, the PIC is learnt to have been standing and leaning behind the co-pilot’s seat. The Airbus A320 had momentarily gone into a “negative G” situation when the PIC and things in the cockpit floated up and those who were not wearing seat belts got injured in the passenger cabin.Also read: Dope test of turbulent Air India flight’s pilot ‘not negative’, sent for confirmation, says government The cabin crew have given a report to AI. The co-pilot may have informed the airline’s ground control about the pilot’s behaviour due to which the unusual step of subjecting the cockpit crew to a drug test — instead of just breath analyser tests — was taken.“AAIB is engaged in systematic collection, preservation and examination of all relevant technical, operational, medical and human-factor evidence,” the govt said.While DGCA is reviewing its rule titled “procedure for examination of aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substances”, India’s senior-most pilots sought a differentiation between a pilot testing positive after having a medication for sleeping or anxiety and those who are found to have consumed “true” psychoactive substances.Airlines have a list of medicines that need to be avoided some hours before flight as they can cause drowsiness.Massive financial losses apart, the airline’s operations and training are again under a cloud, just when it was trying to regain public faith following the Ahmedabad crash in June 2025.While Tatas and partner Singapore Airlines have pumped in thousands of crores and there have been significant cosmetic improvements, it is still looking for leadership and professional management that can usher in the culture required to fly it out of turbulence.
Article Summary: Trouble mounted for the pilot-in-command (PIC) of last Tuesday’s badly rattled Phuket-Delhi Air India flight. It emerged that he had failed the confirmatory dope test and was found to have consumed marijuana. The cabin crew of the flight, AI 2379, has filed a complaint with the airline against the “high’ PIC's onboard behaviour.

Article Title: Tiny plastic pan masala sachets may soon be history
Article Text:
Pan masala may now only be packaged in paper, paperboard, cellulose, or other naturally derived materials (Photo: Agencies).

The rules came into force upon their publication in the gazette

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The tiny plastic sachet that has become synonymous with pan masala may finally be on its way out. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has notified plastic-free packaging norms for the product, a move experts say could further enforcement of an existing ban by allowing the food regulator to act directly against violators.The amended Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2026, require pan masala to be packed only in paper, paperboard, cellulose or other naturally derived materials free from plastic, or in tin or glass containers. The notification prohibits use of materials containing polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, PVC, synthetic polymers, laminates, aluminium foil and metallised layers, and also makes the packaging subject to Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016.A senior FSSAI official told TOI that pan masala has been specifically included under Schedule IV of packaging regulations to provide Food Business Operators with clear guidance on suitable packaging materials, given the widespread use of small single-use packs and the environmental concerns arising from their disposal. However, environmental experts said the notification primarily furthers enforcement rather than imposing fresh prohibition.“The Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, had already placed an explicit legal ban on plastic sachets for gutka, tobacco and pan masala. The FSSAI notification reinforces that mandate through food safety regulations,” said Siddharth G. Singh, programme manager, solid waste management and circular economy, Centre for Science and Environment.He said enforcement of Plastic Waste Management Rules has remained patchy because it largely depends on state pollution control boards and local bodies. Bringing the requirement under the ambit of food safety regulations will allow FSSAI to act directly against Food Business Operators, plugging an enforcement gap that environmental laws alone struggled to address, he said.Singh said pan masala was specifically targeted because the sector relies heavily on use of small single-use sachets, which have a high littering potential and among the lowest collection rates.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has notified plastic- free packaging norms for the product. The move could further enforcement of an existing ban by allowing the food regulator to act directly against violators. The notification prohibits use of materials containing polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, PVC, synthetic polymers, laminates, aluminium foil and metallised layers.

Article Title: Benchmark hospital room cost against 3-star hotel tariff: Panel
Article Text:
Hospital administrators, however, questioned the comparison.

Beyond room rents, the panel, headed by SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav, proposed standardised package rates for common medical and surgical procedures.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A patient’s hospital room in a private hospital could soon cost no more than a room in a nearby three-star hotel if a key recommendation of the parliamentary standing committee on health and family welfare is accepted. In an effort to rein in soaring medical bills, the panel has proposed linking room rents in private hospitals in major metropolitan cities to the average tariff charged by three-star hotels nearby.The recommendation is part of the committee’s report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare facilities in public and private sector, which says the absence of a transparent mechanism for fixing room charges has led to wide variations in bills. It recommended benchmarking room rents to nearby three-star hotels, while allowing hospitals to levy separate charges for resident doctors, nursing care, consumables, meals and laundry.Citing the 80th National Sample Survey (Jan-Dec 2025), the panel said average cost of hospitalisation was Rs 6,631 in govt hospitals compared with Rs 50,508 in private hospitals. For childbirth alone, the average out-of-pocket expenditure was Rs 37,630 in private hospitals against Rs 2,299 in govt facilities.Hospital administrators, however, questioned the comparison. “Hotel room tariffs should not be the yardstick for hospital room rents because medical infra, staffing and support services are different,” said Dr Vinoy Kumar Upadhyay, CMD of Hope Hospital in Greater Noida.Noting the sharp difference in treatment costs, the panel said reducing out-of-pocket expenditure should be a key priority. It called for a legal mechanism to standardise and cap charges for essential treatments and routine procedures in private hospitals, mandatory disclosure of treatment costs before admission, and a fast-track grievance redressal mechanism for complaints related to billing.Beyond room rents, the panel, headed by SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav, proposed standardised package rates for common medical and surgical procedures. It also recommended advance cost estimates for complex treatments, financial navigators to guide patients on treatment costs and insurance, and ‘Continuum of Care’ packages covering screening, treatment and palliative care under a single capped payment. It urged the Centre to raise public health spending to 2.5% of GDP, strengthen govt hospitals, expand affordable medicines, and ensure stricter implementation of the Clinical Establishments Act.
Article Summary: The recommendation is part of the committee’s report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare facilities in public and private sector. It recommended benchmarking room rents to nearby three-star hotels, while allowing hospitals to levy separate charges. Hospital administrators, however, questioned the comparison.

Article Title: States ignore Supreme Court, differ on NEET-PG seat norms
Article Text:
In a representation to PMO in July, a parent sought uniform implementation of the SC judgement

. Some states appear to have implemented the judgement, while others continue with different eligibility conditions.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: More than a year after Supreme Court ruled that residence or domicile cannot be the basis for postgraduate medical admissions under the state quota, parents of NEET-PG aspirants say admission rules still vary across states, leaving students with unequal opportunities despite having taken the same national entrance examination.The concerns stem from SC’s Jan 29, 2025, judgement in Dr Tanvi Behl vs Shrey Goel case, which held that residence-based preference in postgraduate medical admissions is not permissible. The court said admissions should be based on NEET-PG scores while allowing only limited institutional preference, meaning a student may receive preference for having graduated from a particular medical college – and not because he or she is a resident or domicile of a state.The dispute primarily concerns private medical colleges, where admissions are conducted through state counselling. Several states prescribe domicile or other state-specific eligibility conditions. “The intention of the SC judgement was to replace residence-based preference with institutional preference. Some states appear to have implemented the judgement, while others continue with different eligibility conditions.If these policies are challenged, the courts will decide whether they are consistent with the judgement. The Centre can still review the issue and issue uniform guidelines to states,” a health ministry official said.State counselling brochures for the NEET-PG admission process, reviewed by TOI, indeed show differences in eligibility rules. Gujarat requires additional state-specific eligibility conditions for some candidates who completed MBBS outside the state. Maharashtra allows only certain Maharashtra domicile candidates who studied outside the state to apply, while Karnataka permits candidates from other states to participate in counselling, though without Karnataka reservation benefits.Parents say these differences mean students with the same NEET-PG score may not have equal opportunity to compete for PG seats.In a representation to PMO in July, a parent sought uniform implementation of the SC judgement, a common national counselling portal and biannual NEET-PG examinations, arguing that students continue to face unequal admission opportunities across states. PMO has acknowledged the grievance, but no final decision has been communicated.Parents say the system also increases costs as candidates must register separately for multiple counselling processes, each with its own eligibility rules, timelines and security deposits. In response to one representation, NMC said domicile or residence-based reservation under state quota falls within the states’ jurisdiction and advised the complainant to approach the state or UT concerned. A similar representation to PMO in 2022 seeking uniform rules was closed after noting the concerns.
Article Summary: Parents of NEET-PG aspirants say admission rules still vary across states. Concerns stem from SC’s Jan 29, 2025, judgement in Dr Tanvi Behl vs Shrey Goel case. Some states appear to have implemented the judgement, while others continue with different eligibility conditions.

Article Title: Bengal SIR tribunals must work faster: Supreme Court
Article Text:
“The process cannot be so slow that the next assembly elections would be due by the time the appeals are decided,” said CJI Surya Kant.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With nearly 34 lakh appeals pending adjudication before SIR appellate tribunals against deletion of voters’ names in West Bengal, Supreme Court Tuesday decided to take stock of their performance and suggested they speed up their work, saying the process cannot be unending, even though it was unwilling to set a deadline for decision on appeals.“The process cannot be so slow that the next assembly elections would be due by the time the appeals are decided,” said CJI Surya Kant responding to a petition complaining about the slow rate of disposal of appeals by those whose names were deleted from electoral rolls during their Special Intensive Revision (SIR).Petitioner and Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury, through senior advocate Rauf Rahim said the progress in deciding appeals by the tribunals, set up on SC orders, is painfully slow and requires impetus to speed up disposal rate. Chowdhury said names of lakhs of poor people have been deleted from the voter list in Murshidabad and they do not have the wherewithal to approach SC.A bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “These tribunals were constituted on our orders. A substantial time has elapsed since they started working. We must consider their performance keeping in mind the pendency and disposals. Immediate concern is to take stock.”“Once we get the statistics, we would be able to provide it with guidance and information technology to help speed up the process,” Justice Bagchi said. The bench asked Election Commisson to give details of pendency and disposals by Aug 25, the next date of hearing.Also read: Less than 1% appeals disposed of by Bengal SIR tribunals in 100 days When Rahim said appeals are required to be decided early as WB govt has begun depriving deleted voters of benefits of welfare schemes, the bench said this is altogether a separate cause of action which should be adjudicated by Calcutta High Court. “If you expand the scope of this petition, we will send it to HC,” it said and declined to fix a timeline for disposal of appeals.Chowdhury said, “Several people whose names are deleted from voter lists have made appeal before the tribunals and are waiting for the fate of their cases. But the process and infrastructure of the tribunals is not sufficient for early disposal of such a huge number of appeals after giving proper opportunity of hearing.”
Article Summary: Nearly 34 lakh appeals pending adjudication before SIR appellate tribunals against deletion of voters’ names in West Bengal. Supreme Court Tuesday decided to take stock of their performance and suggested they speed up their work. “The process cannot be so slow that the next assembly elections would be due by the time the appeals are decided,” said CJI Surya Kant.

Article Text:
Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult

The legal availability of marijuana for either medicinal or recreational use in places like Thailand and Amsterdam has made life difficult for airlines flying there. The reason: Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult. The only way to deter their consumption by flight crew members, say officials across multiple airlines, is to increase random dope testing, as there substances usually remain present in the body for much longer than alcohol.The concern across airlines globally to check this stems from the fact that operating a flight “under the influence of any psychoactive substance might render (licensed personnel like pilots) unable to safely and properly exercise” perform their duty, as per the International Civil Aviation Organisation.Possibly the most infamous case of this was a US carrier’s off-duty pilot travelling on the jump seat (extra seat behind pilots) in the flight deck trying to shut down the engines. Officials running operations across airlines say the focus in India is primarily on self-reporting and de-addiction.“But given the easy availability of psychoactive substances, we need to make the consequences a bit tougher and act as deterrent. Under DGCA rules, all scheduled commercial airlines and air navigation service providers need to test at least 10% of their flight crew members and air traffic controllers every year.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday asked the Union ministries of home affairs and electronics and information technology to take urgent steps to create a URL-specific and judicially supervised emergency mechanism to protect citizens from grave unlawful digital content.While disposing of a PIL by advocate N K Goswami, a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant said the petitioner in public interest had highlighted the danger from digital threats of violence, doxxing, exposure of minor children’s private details, non-consensual intimate/deepfake content and identity-manipulating digital impersonation.The SC bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said such cyber crimes severely impacted an individual’s right to freedom of speech, the right to dignity, privacy and the right to life.It said the petitioner had highlighted protections against such threats using internet, digital mediums and Artificial Intelligence existing in other countries and suggested to the govt to consider problems highlighted in PIL for urgent remedial measures.Goswami said given the misuse of AI and proliferation of social media and its reach, it was urgently required to create “a constitutionally compliant emergency mechanism against grave unlawful digital harms, namely specific threats, doxxing, unauthorised exposure of children’s private details, non-consensual intimate or Al-generated morphed content, and deepfake/digitally manipulated impersonation causing immediate grave harm”.He said he neither sought a blanket ban on any speech nor suppression of political speech, criticism, satire, parody, journalism, academic comment, public-interest reporting, or legal commentary.

Article Title: Tribunal reforms seek to bring transparency in appointments

NEW DELHI: Tribunal Reforms Bill, piloted by govt in Parliament, is seen as a move that reinforces the constitutional position in appointments: ensuring primacy of the judiciary in deciding top positions. At the same time, it seeks to maintain a three-tier architecture between the tribunal, the secretariat and the administrative ministry with clear roles mapped out for each.In the bill — passed by RS Tuesday and LS Monday — govt has sought to ensure the independence of National Tribunals Commission (NTC) that will supervise the appointment, functioning, discipline and administrative needs of tribunals. To be headed by a retired judge of the Supreme Court or chief justice of a high court, the proposed NTC will have two judicial members drawn from among retired HC judges apart from two technical members. The chairperson and judicial members will be appointed by govt in consultation with the CJI.The commission, through its search and selection committee, has been tasked to streamline selection of chairpersons and members of tribunals. Unlike the current system, where a panel of names is sent, the committee will recommend a single name for each vacancy, along with a waiting list. Strict timelines have been proposed for recommending names to govt and for the Centre to approve them.It addresses a constant complaint that ministries have in appointments getting delayed.Besides, govt has decided to fix the retirement age of chairperson of tribunals at 70 years, with members to retire at 67, unless they complete their five-year terms.The commission will be assisted by a secretariat with the administrative ministry having no role in either advertising for the post or scrutinising the candidates. The ministry concerned will merely forward inputs to the secretariat on the candidate and Intelligence Bureau will provide its reports. Officials argued that this will end any possible conflict of interest that the ministry concerned will have as a litigant.
Article Summary: Tribunal Reforms Bill, piloted by govt in Parliament, is seen as a move that reinforces the constitutional position in appointments. NEW DELHI: The Centre should scrap all existing inter-state border check posts within six months and replace the All India Tourist Permit with a unified All India Passenger Permit within a year, a parliamentary panel has recommended, pitching for a sweeping overhaul of the country’s bus transport system.The committee headed by JD(U) MP Sanjay Kumar Jha made the recommendations after consultations with govt departments, bus operators, passengers and other stakeholders to identify key hurdles facing the sector, which transports more passengers daily than Indian Railways.The panel noted that India has around 4.4 lakh buses, but only about 1.1 lakh are owned by govt entities, mainly state road transport undertakings. Ten states account for nearly 90% of these govt-owned buses, including Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.Calling for an overhaul of the permit regime, panel urged road transport ministry to replace the All India Tourist Permit with an All India Passenger Permit. The new permit should reflect the number of passengers actually carried, ensuring that enforcement does not hinge on whether a traveller qualifies as a “tourist”.“The rights of the permit holder, including the right to halt, to board and set down passengers at notified points, and to enter public terminals on payment, should be stated exhaustively on the face of the permit,” panel said.It also asked Centre to prevail upon six states to close border check posts that they are still operating.Panel further recommended that all bus terminals provide private operators “non-discriminatory access” to pick up passengers on payment of an entry fee, following the model at Delhi’s ISBT.It also proposed establishment of a National Bus Terminals Authority to develop and standardise terminal infrastructure and, where states agree, manage bus terminals and intermodal passenger hubs.Panel further recommended a unified online ticketing platform covering state-run and private bus operators for passenger convenience.It has proposed a citizen vigilance channel, modelled on Election Commission’s cVIGIL app, allowing passengers to file geo-tagged, time-stamped complaints—with photos or videos—about overloading, unsafe transport of schoolchildren, faulty safety equipment and poor sanitation in buses, terminals and halting points.Complaints would be automatically forwarded to the enforcement authority concerned for action within a prescribed timeframe, it said.

NEW DELHI: India's food safety regulator has barred the use of plastic and plastic-laminated packaging for pan masala, under an amendment aimed at tightening existing packaging norms, according to a press release.The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has specified that pan masala may now only be packaged in paper, paperboard, cellulose, or other naturally derived materials. Such materials must be entirely free of plastic, including polyethene, polypropylene, polyester, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and other synthetic polymers, copolymers or laminates, as well as aluminium foil or metallised layers, the release said. Tin and glass containers continue to be permitted, it added.The press release further stated that packaging will also need to conform to clauses (f) and (i) of sub-rule 1 of rule 4 of the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, framed under the Environment Protection Act, 1986.The amendment has been incorporated as a new entry in Schedule IV of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018, which lists suggested packaging materials. It has been placed right after the existing entries at Serial Number 10, the release said.Notified as the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Amendment Regulations, 2026, the amendment will come into force from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette, according to the release.The regulations were issued by FSSAI in exercise of powers conferred under clause (k) of sub-section (2) of Section 92 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and with prior approval of the Central Government, the release said.
Article Summary: India's food safety regulator has barred the use of plastic and plastic- laminated packaging for pan masala. Pan masala may now only be packaged in paper, paperboard, cellulose, or other naturally derived materials. Tin and glass containers continue to be permitted.

Heavy monsoon rains continued to disrupt life across Himachal Pradesh, with 204 roads blocked, 70 people killed in rain-related incidents and damage to public property estimated at more than Rs 910 crore over the past 43 days, according to the latest State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC) assessment.The assessment covers the period from June 30 to August 11 and captures the impact of repeated heavy rainfall, landslides, cloudbursts and other weather-related incidents across the hill state.According to SEOC data, 70 people have died in direct disaster-related incidents since June 30. Landslides accounted for 14 deaths, while 23 people died after falling from steep slopes, rocks or trees. Seven deaths were caused by snake bites, six by electrocution and four by cloudbursts.Lahaul and Spiti reported the highest number of direct disaster-related deaths at 14, followed by Kangra with 12.The wider toll has also been compounded by road accidents. As many as 93 people have died in road accidents during the same period, with Chamba reporting 16 fatalities, followed by Kullu (13), Sirmaur (12) and Shimla (11), as reproted by ANI.Meanwhile, cumulative damage to public property has reached around Rs 910.35 crore.The Public Works Department has suffered the biggest losses, estimated at Rs 686.36 crore, while damage to the power sector stands at around Rs 203.90 crore.The monsoon has also damaged houses, other private structures, livestock and crops across the state's 12 districts, adding to losses for affected households.Mandi is the worst affected in terms of road connectivity, with 80 roads currently blocked. The Mandi-Kullu route has also been disrupted at Jalogi Dwada. Kullu has reported 56 blocked roads, while 23 roads remain closed in Sirmaur. Two national highways — NH-154 and NH-21 — are also among the affected routes.The road closures have disrupted inter-district connectivity and complicated the movement of essential supplies and emergency response teams.The monsoon has also damaged the state's power and drinking water infrastructure. Forty-five distribution transformer regions are currently out of service, including 41 in Sirmaur's Nahan subdivision.Around 82 drinking water supply schemes have been affected across the state. Sirmaur accounts for 31 of the disrupted schemes, followed by Hamirpur with 11 and Mandi with eight.Authorities and emergency response teams are continuing restoration work, including clearing landslides and debris, reopening roads and restoring power and water supply. However, persistent rainfall and the risk of further landslides continue to hamper relief and restoration efforts.
Article Summary: Lahaul and Spiti reported the highest number of direct disaster-related deaths at 14, followed by Kangra with 12. As many as 93 people have died in road accidents during the same period. Public Works Department has suffered the biggest losses, estimated at Rs 686.36 crore.

Article Title: Climate change, human activity driving Himalayan extreme weather, Centre tells Lok Sabha

NEW DELHI: Climate change is making extreme rainfall events in the Himalayan region more frequent and intense, while human activity is also increasing the risk of disasters, the Centre told the Lok Sabha on Tuesday, as reported by news agency PTI.Minister of state for home affairs Nityanand Rai said assessments by weather experts, scientific institutions and state authorities had found a link between climate change and the worsening intensity and frequency of extreme rainfall events in the Himalayas.The response came to a question on whether climate change and unscientific construction were contributing to the rising incidence of cloudbursts and other disasters in Himachal Pradesh.Rai cited findings of a Multi-Sectoral Central Team (MSCT), which was formed to examine the increasing frequency and severity of cloudbursts, flash floods, landslides and extreme rainfall in the state. The team includes experts from the National Disaster Management Authority, Central Building Research Institute, Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, IIT Indore and other agencies.Inputs from the India Meteorological Department, Central Water Commission and Geological Survey of India have also been considered as part of the assessment.The MSCT is examining the causes behind the increase in extreme weather events, including the geographical and ground conditions of the worst-hit areas and data provided by various government agencies. It will also recommend long-term steps to reduce the impact of such disasters, Rai said.The Centre said faster snowmelt was another factor contributing to increased runoff in high-altitude areas. Rapid melting can send large volumes of water into already vulnerable mountain terrain, increasing downstream flows.The government also flagged moraine instability as a factor behind off-season slope failures and heavy runoff. Moraines are deposits of loose rock, soil and other debris left behind by glaciers, which can become unstable and trigger slope failures and the movement of water and debris.
Article Summary: Climate change is making extreme rainfall events in the Himalayan region more frequent and intense. Human activity is also increasing the risk of disasters, the Centre told the Lok Sabha on Tuesday. The response came to a question on whether climate change and unscientific construction were contributing to the rising incidence of cloudbursts and other disasters.

Article Title: Centre likely to send FCRA Bill to JPC amid opposition
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Centre is likely to send the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) Amendment Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) for detailed scrutiny, amid objections from Christian representatives and opposition parties, news agency ANI reported citing sources.The Bill, introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25, seeks to amend the FCRA, 2010, which regulates the acceptance and utilisation of foreign contributions by individuals, associations and companies in India.Although the Bill has not yet been listed for consideration and passage in the Lok Sabha, the government had earlier indicated that it could be taken up on August 12.According to sources, Christian representatives met Union home minister Amit Shah and sought either withdrawal of the Bill or its referral to a JPC, citing concerns over its provisions.The development follows a meeting between Mizoram chief minister Lalduhoma and Shah, during which the chief minister raised regional concerns and submitted recommendations on the proposed legislation. Lalduhoma was accompanied by Reverend John Raldosanga, chairman of the Mizoram Kohhran Hruaitu Committee (MKHC), and Reverend Lalhmangaiha, general secretary of the Council of Churches in Mizoram (CCM)."The only thing that is very clearly mentioned to us is that it's not going to be retrospective.That assurance was given to us, and the rest of the points will be given a paragraph-wise comment by him... the discussion on the 12th of this month in Parliament," Lalduhoma had said.Separately, a delegation led by DMK leader P Wilson met Shah and submitted a memorandum raising concerns that the proposed legislation "impacts religious minorities and civil society".The delegation also flagged provisions including Section 14B and Chapter IIIA, arguing that delays on the FCRA Online Portal or minor technical non-compliances could lead to automatic cessation of registration and trigger the provisional or permanent vesting of assets with a state-notified Designated Authority.A major proposed change is the creation of a Designated Authority to oversee foreign contributions and assets belonging to organisations whose FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or ceases to remain valid.Under the proposed provisions, an organisation losing its FCRA registration would initially have its foreign contributions and assets vested provisionally with the Designated Authority. If its registration is restored or renewed within the prescribed period, the assets and unused foreign funds would be returned. Otherwise, the assets could vest permanently with the authority.The Bill also provides for cessation of an FCRA certificate following its expiry, non-renewal or refusal of renewal, including in cases where an organisation becomes defunct or its registration ceases.For assets such as places of worship, the proposed law requires the Designated Authority to preserve their religious character. It also provides for revision and judicial appeal against orders issued by the authority.The Bill proposes changes to the penalty framework as well, including reducing the maximum imprisonment for violations from five years to one year. It further proposes that state agencies obtain prior approval from the Centre before launching investigations under the FCRA.Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu assembly adopted a state government sponsored resolution urging the Centre to withdraw the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill, alleging it may adversely affect the autonomy of charitable organisations and functioning of institutions run by minorities.The monsoon session of Parliament began on July 20 and is scheduled to conclude on August 13. Proceedings have repeatedly been disrupted by opposition protests over several issues, including Delhi Police action against protesters on July 20. Several Bills have been passed in the Lok Sabha amid opposition protests and limited debate.
Article Summary: The Centre is likely to send the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) Amendment Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee. Christian representatives met Union home minister Amit Shah and sought either withdrawal of the Bill or its referral to a JPC. NEW DELHI: Isha Foundation founder Sadhguru on Monday launched a new photography book called "Disappearing Faces", featuring photographs of people he encountered during his journeys through the remote Himalayas of Nepal and Tibet.Published by Penguin India, the book was launched by Union minister Mansukh Mandaviya at the India International Centre in New Delhi.The launch was followed by a conversation between Sadhguru and commentator Anand Ranganathan, exploring the stories and experiences behind the photographs featured in the book.“These faces represent an era that will soon disappear: faces etched only by sensory perception of light and darkness, heat and cold, of springs and winters - above all, uncontaminated by information that is disconnected from our senses. Our senses lead to a certain sense of life where there is no Non-sense," Sadhguru said during the conversation."These are the visages that represent life that seems rudimentary but is rich with strong experiences of the land, the winds, the waters and the people. Over the last five decades, year after year, beyond the beauty and wondrous nature of the mountains, these faces have drawn me into the deep crevices of the Himalayas," he added.Carrying a camera along the way, Sadhguru began documenting faces shaped by a life lived close to nature and increasingly distant from the cities.The book offers an intimate visual record of the people Sadhguru encountered during his journeys.Sadhguru first journeyed to Manasarovar and Mount Kailash in 2006 and has since returned repeatedly, leading seekers on the Himalayan pilgrimage. After undertaking his first motorcycle journey to Kailash in 2025, Sadhguru is set to return once again this year on a motorcycle, continuing his unique engagement with the sacred landscape of the Himalayas.The Himalayas have remained a significant part of Sadhguru’s life over the years, alongside his efforts towards human wellbeing, raising human consciousness and his commitment to ecological regeneration.
Article Summary: Isha Foundation founder Sadhguru launches a new photography book called "Disappearing Faces" The book features photographs of people he encountered during his journeys through the remote Himalayas of Nepal and Tibet. The book was launched by Union minister Mansukh Mandaviya at the India International Centre.

Article Title: Attendance shortfall: Law students get one-time Bombay HC nod to take exams for academic year 2025-26
Article Text:
In a huge relief to students of ILS Law college in Pune barred from appearing for their semester-end law exams for attendance shortfall, Bombay high court on Monday permitted them to appear for the exams.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: In a huge relief to students of ILS Law college in Pune barred from appearing for their semester-end law exams in the academic year 2025-26 for attendance shortfall, Bombay high court on Monday permitted them to appear for the exams as a “strictly one-time measure’’. Justices Riyaz Chagla and Farhan Dubash relied on a recent July 21 Supreme Court order that permitted students as a one-time relief to appear for their examinations in the academic year 20-26.The HC clarified that its relief would apply to all similarly barred students of the college who had not filed petitions, as it said the SC order had carved out similar placed students as a “protected class’’. But the bench clarified its order was “confined to the academic session 2025–26’’.The HC said its order cannot be construed as diluting the attendance rules for any other academic session. “Students pursuing legal education shall continue to remain bound by the attendance requirements otherwise applicable to them,’’ the bench said.The HC order came in a batch of petitions filed by 41 students pursuing different years of the 3-year and 5-year law courses conducted at ILS, Pune affiliated to the Savitribai Phule Pune University.The University said their attendance was tween 46 to 54 % while minimum attendance was 75 %.The petitions said an earlier 70 % rule with 20 % additional waiver rule ought to apply to them and also cited a November 3 2025 Delhi HC order to argue their case.The Delhi HC High Court directed that no student enrolled in a recognised law college in India should be detained or prevented from appearing for examinations or from pursuing academic progression solely on account of shortage of attendance.The SC then stayed the Delhi HC order, prospectively in May. But in July protected students across colleges against a lost academic year of 2025-26, with a one-time reprieve to appear for the final exam in that academic year when the Delhi HC order was passed. The SC order does not prescribe any minimum attendance for the protected class of last academic year student, HC noted.On Monday, disposing of the batch of petitions the Bombay HC clarified that the Delhi HC order did not bind it, but the July SC order did.Six different HCs had differed with Delhi HC.The Pune University and the law college argued that the SC order would apply only to final examination students of the 3 year and 5 year LLB courses. But disagreeing, the HC reasoned and the SC meant “concluding exam for that academic session’’ hence the petitioners who were students of first, second, third- or fourth-year stand included.The HC said, “A student studying in an earlier year who is prevented from appearing for the semester-end examination may equally lose the academic session and, consequently, be unable to progress to the succeeding academic year’’ If the apex court “ intended to protect only students in the final year or final semester of the law course, it could readily have said so,’’ the HC explained.The HC clarified it has not dealt with the controversy raised by the students of whether the maximum condonation of 20% contemplated under Ordinance 70 was required to operate upon the minimum attendance requirement of 70% prescribed under Rule 12 of the Legal Education Rules or upon the requirement of 75% prescribed under Ordinance 68. This issue is left open.The HC had earlier granted interim protection to the Petitioners who appeared for their examinations and confirmed the relief. The HC directed the University to conduct supplementary exams within 4 weeks for academic year 2025-26 for those who could not appear.
Article Summary: Bombay high court on Monday permitted students of ILS Law college in Pune barred from appearing for their semester-end law exams for attendance shortfall. Justices Riyaz Chagla and Farhan Dubash relied on a recent July 21 Supreme Court order that permitted students as a one-time relief to appear for their examinations.

Article Title: Air India CEO meets MoCA, DGCA amid Phuket flight turbulence probe

NEW DELHI: Air India's outgoing CEO reportedly met government officials on Tuesday amid the ongoing row after the Delhi-Phuket flight turbulence incident.The airlines' outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson met senior officials of MoCA and DGCA regarding the flight that suddenly lost about 300 feet of altitude last week, reported PTI, citing sources. The sources said the civil aviation ministry called the three senior airline executives for a meeting in the wake of the August 4 incident.Executive advisor to Tata Sons Chairman and former Civil Aviation Secretary Pradeep Singh Kharola as well as Air India's Head of Flight Safety Deepak Joshi also attended the meeting, they said.However, Reuters reported, citing sources that the civil aviation ​minister has ​summoned the CEO. No confirmation has come from the airlines or the government.Although, as Campbell was leaving, after meeting thesenior officials of MoCA and DGCA, he said, "We were just giving an update on the status of the investigation...It is up to him (MoCA Minister) to give an update."The meeting comes a day after the government advanced a probe into the incident, which involved the Airbus A320 suddenly losing about 300 feet of altitude during the flight.The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has classified the incident as serious and is examining the circumstances surrounding the sudden descent.The pilot-in-command is also under scrutiny after his psychoactive substance screening test on arrival was found to be “not negative”. The sample has been sent to a designated laboratory for confirmatory testing, with the final report awaited, the aviation ministry said.“Further action, as appropriate, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation and confirmatory test results,” the ministry said.Under DGCA rules, a pilot whose initial screening is non-negative must be immediately removed from safety-sensitive duties until the confirmatory report is received. Both pilots of the August 4 Air India flight have been taken off flying duty pending the investigation.The AI 2379 flight was carrying 145 people from Phuket to Delhi when it suddenly lost altitude, injuring passengers and crew. The aircraft landed safely in Delhi, but 17 people were hospitalised.The AAIB probe is examining both possible mechanical issues and pilot behaviour. Investigators are also expected to analyse the aircraft's flight data and cockpit voice recorders to establish the sequence of events.
Article Summary: Air India's outgoing CEO reportedly met government officials on Tuesday amid the ongoing row after the Delhi-Phuket flight turbulence incident. NEW DELHI: As India gears up to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on Aug 15, three Russian cosmonauts on board the International Space Station have extended their I-Day greetings to the Indian people by holding the tricolour and sending a special video message recalling decades-old friendship between Moscow and New Delhi. The message transmitted from the space station from an altitude of 408 km serves as a masterclass in orbital diplomacy.In the video message reposted by the Embassy of Russia in India on Monday, Russian space crew — Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Andrey Fedyaev — congratulated India and described space exploration as a key pillar of bilateral ties. “Eight decades ago, India broke free from colonial rule and embarked on a journey towards self-reliance and prosperity... Dear friends, today the Republic of India is celebrating its 80th Independence Day,” cosmonaut Pyotr Dubrov said, extending his wishes to India.Holding the tricolour alongside three posters showcasing India-Russia space cooperation, the space crew highlighted key milestones in the Indo-Russian partnership, including the 1975 launch of India’s Aryabhata satellite and 1984 flight of India-born cosmonaut Rakesh Sharma.The cosmonauts also talked about India’s most-ambitious ongoing Gaganyaan programme, noting four Indian astronauts (Gaganauts) were trained in Russia — Prashanth Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap, and Shubhanshu Shukla completed their space training module at Russia's Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre in Star City between Feb 2020 and March 2021.Anna Kikina recalled Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin’s historic visit to India in Nov 1961. She quoted Gagarin’s famous words about the country: “India is very beautiful from above, but it is even more beautiful and special because it is home to true friends.”“The friendship between our countries has been time-tested, and space exploration is one of the main areas of our cooperation,” she said.
Article Summary: Three Russian cosmonauts on board the International Space Station have extended their I-Day greetings to the Indian people. Russian space crew — Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Andrey Fedyaev — congratulated India. NEW DELHI: Rahul Navin has been granted a one-year extension as ED director as his two-year fixed tenure was due to end this month.The tenure of Navin, a 1993-batch Indian Revenue Service (I-T) officer, as director of enforcement has been extended for a period of one year beyond "13.08.2026 i.e. up to 13.08.2027, including extension in service beyond the date of his superannuation or until further orders," as per DoPT.After three years as ED director, he could get two more extensions and serve till August 2029, all through the PM Modi government's tenure, with polls due in April-May 2029.Navin's tenure as director (in-charge) began on September 15, 2023, and he was appointed as ED director on August 14, 2024, while his service retirement was due on July 31, 2027. He has set a roadmap for officers to complete probes within two years and ensure attached properties are auctioned and restituted to rightful claimants and fraud victims, including banks or individuals.
Article Summary: Rahul Navin has been granted a one-year extension as ED director. His two-year fixed tenure was due to end this month. He could get two more extensions and serve till August 2029, with polls due in April-May 2029.

NEW DELHI: Days after the Supreme Court gave former prime minister Manmohan Singh a clean chit in the coal block allocation case, senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi on Tuesday invoked former PM's legacy and attacked the Narendra Modi government.Sonia said Singh's record of integrity and accountability was in stark contrast to the way the Modi government has functioned. She said history would remember Singh as a quiet, gentle but "highly consequential prime minister."Taking a dig at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Sonia said that since he is currently "forgiving" students who attacked him, he could also use the opportunity to forgive himself for his "undignified slander" against Singh.The Congress parliamentary party chairperson said the Supreme Court judgment ended what she described as one of the most tragic episodes in public discourse -- the "witch-hunt against Dr Singh, a man of the most remarkable probity and integrity.""The lobby against him was coordinated and well-organised, with actors stretching from the bureaucracy to the media, the judiciary, civil society, and most certainly to the RSS and BJP.Today, their bogus crusade has come to its inevitable conclusion of nothingness. Dr Singh has been vindicated on every count," Sonia said in an article published in The Indian Express.Also read: Coal block scam case in Supreme Court: Ex-PM Manmohan Singh gets clean chit two years after his death Sonia said July 29, 2026, was an important but largely unacknowledged date in India's recent political history. On that day, the Supreme Court upheld the CBI's clean chit to Singh in the alleged coal block allocation scam.She also pointed out that the Supreme Court criticised the trial court for rejecting the CBI's closure reports and making adverse remarks against Singh without any "compelling reason".Sonia said Singh's record of integrity and accountability stood in contrast to what she called as the Modi government's "misuse of agencies" such as the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the CBI."Its purpose has been to exert pressure on politicians. Leaders are either silenced through coercion or cynically folded into the BJP or, in some remarkable instances, rewarded with ministerial positions as well."When credible accusations of corruption emerge, the Modi government simply brushes them aside. Corrupt when you're in the Opposition, suddenly clean when you jump ship!" Sonia said.Sonia also said it was not a coincidence that Modi was among the most vocal critics of Singh."His snide and atrocious remarks in the Rajya Sabha on February 8, 2017, that only Dr Singh knew 'the art of bathing with a raincoat on', will go down as the lowest point of our parliamentary history," former Congress president said."Introspection, like charity, must begin from home. Ultimately, the attack on Dr Singh was motivated by a desperate desire to shift the public conversation and narrative away from his outstanding governance record," she added.Sonia highlighted Singh's economic record, saying his government brought major economic changes, high growth rates and a rise in consumption and private investment.She said India also showed resilience during the 2008 global financial crisis."Let us not forget that in spite of the reworking of how the growth of India's GDP is calculated, the 10 years of the UPA government saw higher economic growth than the past 12 years, resulting in millions being pulled out of poverty," Sonia said.She also highlighted several welfare and social justice initiatives introduced during Singh's tenure.According to Sonia, the Manmohan Singh government delivered the constitutional promise of the Right to Education and expanded OBC reservation in centrally funded higher education institutions, including the IITs and IIMs."The Forest Rights Act recognised the ancestral rights of our Adivasi and forest-dwelling communities, after a decades-long struggle. The MGNREGA, recently demolished by the Modi government, was the most powerful social security intervention set up anywhere," she said.Sonia also cited the National Food Security Act, 2013, as another major achievement of Singh's government. The law guaranteed access to basic food rations for crores of families.She said civil society became stronger during Singh's tenure and people could protest against the government and prime minister.Sonia also claimed that Singh regularly remained accountable to Parliament and the media through more than 100 unscripted press conferences."And of course, we cannot forget that the landmark and path-breaking Indo-US nuclear deal, which overturned decades of nuclear discrimination against and denial towards India and marked our arrival on the global stage, was possible because of his political courage and sustained initiative," she said.Sonia said the allegations against Singh's integrity had now been exposed as baseless and that his record was increasingly being recognised as a period of economic, political and social progress."We all certainly regret that he is not here to see this day and to guide the nation with his wisdom. But it is a solace to us all that his prophetic prediction of January 2014 is becoming increasingly self-evident with every passing day."History will indeed remember him kindly as a quiet, gentle but a most consequential prime minister," Sonia said.Her remarks came after the Supreme Court closed the criminal case against Singh by setting aside a summoning order against him.Singh, who died on December 27, 2024, now stands formally acquitted in the high-profile criminal case.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi hails former PM Manmohan Singh after SC clean chit in coal block allocation case. She said Singh's record of integrity and accountability was in stark contrast to the way the Modi government has functioned. Sonia said history would remember Singh as a quiet, gentle but "highly consequential prime minister"

KOLKATA: The West Bengal Assembly is set to consider changes in the Kolkata and Howrah municipal corporations, bringing the city's civic politics into focus today. HYDERABAD: Growth of urban transport in Hyderabad and a high-profile police case figure among key issues today. How human composting works

A new option for Maryland families

The debate around a different kind of farewell

Maryland is giving residents a new option for what happens to their bodies after death. According to WYPR, a public radio station serving Maryland, the state is now home to what is described as the nation's largest human composting facility: a 37,000-square-foot facility in Elkridge operated by Earth Funeral. The facility uses a process formally known as natural organic reduction, offering an alternative to conventional burial and cremation.Human composting may sound unusual, but the basic idea is rooted in the natural decomposition of organic material. Instead of placing a body underground or exposing it to the high temperatures of cremation, natural organic reduction uses a controlled environment to accelerate the body's natural breakdown and eventually produce soil-like material.The process takes place inside specially designed vessels, where bacteria, fungi and organic materials such as mulch help break down the remains over roughly a month. At the end of the process, about 300 pounds of soil remain. The bones are pulverised and added to the soil, which can then be returned to the family or placed in land-conservation projects.Maryland is among the states that have legalised natural organic reduction, allowing the service to become available to residents.Earth Funeral recently opened its Elkridge facility, creating a new human-composting option for people on the East Coast.According to WYPR, the facility is nearly 37,000 square feet and is described as the nation's largest human-composting facility. The facility was designed to make the service more accessible to people on the East Coast, who previously may have had to transport remains long distances to reach a human composting facility. This option is also emerging as part of a wider discussion about the environmental impact of traditional funeral practices. Traditional burial requires land and may involve embalming fluids and caskets. Cremation eliminates the need for a burial plot but relies on combustion and produces emissions.Natural organic reduction takes a different approach by allowing the body to return to the natural material cycle. The resulting soil can be returned to families or placed in land-conservation projects, subject to Maryland's regulations.The arrival of human composting in Maryland also reflects changing attitudes toward death and end-of-life planning. For some people, the attraction is environmental: they want their final disposition to use fewer resources and avoid a permanent burial space. For others, the idea of becoming part of the natural landscape provides a meaningful alternative to conventional funeral traditions.The practice remains relatively new in the United States. Washington became the first state to legalise natural organic reduction in 2019, and Maryland is among a growing number of states that have since approved it. Availability, regulations and the rules governing the use or scattering of the resulting soil vary by state. For Maryland, however, the opening of the Elkridge facility expands the choices available for end-of-life arrangements. What was once an option accessible only in a limited number of places is now available in the state, giving residents and people in the wider region another choice.Rather than viewing death only through the traditional choices of burial or cremation, natural organic reduction offers another possibility: allowing the body to decompose in a carefully controlled setting and ultimately be transformed into soil-like material. For families interested in a lower-impact approach, Maryland's new facility represents a distinctly different way of saying goodbye.
